_comment: Generation and fuels. Data centers live in their own repository,
datacenter_yt, because a data center is demand rather than generation and
because on its own it sweeps every Oklahoma place in under two weeks.
The codebook is identical in both on purpose, so the two exports carry the
same columns and can be stacked in a spreadsheet and compared directly.
This one runs Mondays, datacenter_yt runs Thursdays. The YouTube quota
belongs to the Google Cloud project rather than the repository, so sharing
one API key across both means they must not run on the same day.
Counties come from the news crawler, which pulls them out of
headlines. Set url to null to use only the hand-written list below.
Counties are rotated across runs so the search budget is not blown
on the same ones every week.

1. Subject. A topic phrase has to appear in the title or description.
2. Local signal. It has to be tied to somewhere in the United States:

_topics_comment: Two tiers, because 77 counties times seven technologies is 539 searches and
statewide runs every week for every technology, so anything that makes the
Oklahoma news is caught within a week.
county_template is rotated: each run takes the next county_block pairs of
county and technology and works through them, picking up where it left off.
A full cycle takes a few months and runs in the background.
Set county_template to null for a topic with too little volume to be worth
_cities_comment: Oklahoma counties mostly do not zone; municipalities do. A data center or
battery site near a town is decided by a city council, and the coverage is
titled 'Norman city council', never 'Cleveland County'. So cities are
searched alongside counties and go into the same rotation.
Cities also count as a local signal in their own right, so a clip about
Yukon from a channel with no call letters is still recognized as local.
_places_comment: A topic may carry its own places list. Hydropower and disposal wells are
geographically concentrated — the dam fight is around Grand Lake, the
earthquakes are in the belt north of Oklahoma City — so sweeping all 127
places for them would spend most of the budget asking counties with no
dam and no disposal wells. Leave places out and the topic sweeps
everywhere, which is right for transmission because lines cross the state.
_schedule_comment: Runs five days a week, Wednesday through Sunday. Nothing else touches the
YouTube quota on those days: elsa_yt has Monday and datacenter_yt Tuesday.
Wednesday runs the statewide searches plus a 48-place block. Thursday
through Sunday skip the statewide searches, which would only repeat the
same results, and spend the whole 95-search budget on the sweep instead.
That is 48 + 4x95 = 428 place-technology pairs a week against 662 in a
full cycle, so a cycle takes about a week and a half rather than twelve.
